plan.title: BFA in Motion Pictures & Television
plan.notes: Academy of Art University measures progress in semester UNITS (the school's own term); all courses are 3 units and units are recorded here as credits. Source: the school's official program page (Core Classes carousel + Degree Requirements unit table + named general-education requirements), hand-transcribed 2026-10-01. Each BFA page publishes a 10-course 'Core Classes' carousel and a Degree Requirements table of Core 24 + Sophomore Portfolio 3 + Senior Portfolio 3 + Major 39 + Electives 9 + Liberal Arts 42 = 120 units. To reconcile both as printed, the portfolio-titled carousel courses are applied to the portfolio lines and the remaining 8 form Core 24 (see program-specific note). Major 39 is modeled as 13 'Major Elective' choice slots: the public pages name no specific major electives (they vary by emphasis/specialization and are chosen with an advisor). Electives 9 is 3 generic choice slots. Liberal Arts 42 is the page's named general-education requirements plus 'Liberal Arts Elective' choice slots to reach 42. The school publishes NO term-by-term map and NO course-level prerequisites on its public pages; the 8 semesters below are an editorial 15-unit/semester sequencing and all prereq lists are empty. Degree requirements: minimum grade of C- in all major coursework; minimum 2.0 GPA. Source is the school's own staging mirror (1wwwcleandev.academyart.edu), which renders the same official program-page template; the live-site equivalent page was not located in this pass. Portfolio reconciliation: the carousel shows 10 courses while the Degree Requirements table lists Core 24. The page names no portfolio course explicitly; MPT 495 (Into the Industry, the only 400-level carousel course, the senior capstone whose program outcomes include the Final Review demo reel) is applied to the Senior Portfolio line and MPT 234 (Scene Production Laboratory, the 200-level production lab matching the Midpoint Review) to the Sophomore Portfolio line, as editorial readings so the plan matches the school's published unit table - confirm with an advisor. Students specialize in directing, producing, cinematography, editing, production design, or screenwriting (the Major Elective slots).
